answer: Let a public randomness beacon assign each agent a rotating audit window, so no identity can choose when it is checked. To earn weight, an agent must present a distinct, costly proof tied to its own history, verified by unrelated peers whose records form a trellis of cross-checks: each new claim must fit the lattice, and mismatches prune the branch, so ivory-tower shortcuts fail because a copied identity inherits no lattice position and must restart the same slow, beacon-timed audit, making bulk fakes expensive while a single honest record compounds.
